title: One Beat, One Miss — Seoul's Big Rally Meets a Split Night in New York
body:
Wednesday was a day when Korean investors finally had something to cheer about. The KOSPI soared 6.6% to 6,012.44, a **remarkable** jump that lifted the index back above the 6,000 mark, while SK hynix, which reported its quarterly results that morning, surged 10.9%. Foreign investors and institutions bought a combined 1.78 trillion won of shares, whereas individuals sold 1.80 trillion won.

Across the Pacific, however, the picture was far less clear. The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4% in a 10-2 vote, and both **dissents** (반대표) came from officials who wanted a quarter-point hike. If those two had won the vote, the Fed would have raised borrowing costs instead of holding them steady. By doing little to push back on talk of a December hike, the statement **left the door open** to one. Big Tech then sent two very different signals **simultaneously**. Microsoft delivered an **upside surprise**, earning $4.89 a share against an expected $4.72, and its stock rose about 4% in **after-hours** trading. Alphabet, by contrast, **fell short of** forecasts, with earnings of $2.12 versus $3.01, and its shares slid about 6%. Although the S&P 500 ended the regular session up just 0.3%, the late moves were far larger. Consequently, Thursday's trading in Seoul, where chip stocks lead the market, may depend on which report investors take more seriously.
ko:
수요일은 한국 투자자들이 마침내 반길 거리가 생긴 날이었다. 코스피는 6.6% 급등한 6,012.44로 마감해 지수를 다시 6,000선 위로 끌어올리는 놀라운 상승을 보였고, 그날 아침 분기 실적을 발표한 SK하이닉스는 10.9% 치솟았다. 외국인과 기관은 합쳐서 1조 7,800억 원어치 주식을 순매수한 반면, 개인은 1조 8,000억 원어치를 순매도했다.

그러나 태평양 건너편의 그림은 훨씬 덜 분명했다. 연준은 10대 2 표결로 기준금리를 3.75~4%로 동결했는데, 반대표 두 장은 모두 0.25%p 인상을 원한 위원들에게서 나왔다. 만약 그 두 사람이 표결에서 이겼다면 연준은 금리를 동결하는 대신 올렸을 것이다. 성명서가 12월 인상론을 거의 반박하지 않으면서 인상 가능성을 열어 두었다. 이어서 빅테크는 서로 전혀 다른 두 신호를 동시에 보냈다. 마이크로소프트는 주당 4.89달러를 벌어 예상치 4.72달러를 웃도는 깜짝 호실적을 냈고, 주가는 시간외 거래에서 약 4% 올랐다. 반면 알파벳은 주당순이익 2.12달러로 예상치 3.01달러에 못 미쳤고 주가는 약 6% 미끄러졌다. S&P500은 정규장을 0.3% 상승에 그치며 마쳤지만, 장 마감 뒤 움직임은 훨씬 컸다. 따라서 반도체주가 시장을 이끄는 서울의 목요일 장은 투자자들이 어느 실적을 더 무겁게 받아들이느냐에 달려 있을 수 있다.

vocab.en_easy: An official disagreement with a decision that most others support.
vocab.ex: There were two dissents at the Fed meeting, so the vote was 10-2.

vocab.en_easy: A result that turns out better than people expected.
vocab.ex: The jobs report was an upside surprise, and stocks jumped right after it came out.

vocab.en_easy: Happening after the normal trading session has closed.
vocab.ex: Alphabet fell about 6% in after-hours trading, so I checked the futures before I went to bed.

vocab.en_easy: Unusual or surprising in a way that makes people notice.
vocab.ex: Honestly, my progress on deadlifts this month has been remarkable — I added 20 kilos.
I try not to do cardio and heavy squats simultaneously, so I split them into different days.

vocab.en_easy: To fail to reach a goal, number, or expectation.
vocab.ex: My run yesterday fell short of my goal by about half a kilometer.

vocab.en_easy: To keep a possibility alive instead of ruling it out.
vocab.ex: I said no to the trip for now, but I left the door open to joining them next month.

grammar.point: 가정법 과거완료 (If + had p.p., 주어 + would have p.p.)
grammar.quote: If those two had won the vote, the Fed would have raised borrowing costs instead of holding them steady.
grammar.explain_ko: 이미 지나간 과거 사실(실제로는 2명이 졌다)을 반대로 가정한다. If절은 had p.p., 주절은 would/could/might have p.p. — '만약 ~했다면 ~했을 텐데'. 시제가 하나씩 뒤로 밀린다는 점(과거 일인데 had won)이 핵심. 수능 어법에서 주절을 would raise(가정법 과거)로 바꿔 틀리게 내는 경우가 많다.
examples: If I had bought the dip last week, I would have made a nice profit yesterday.
(OPIc) If I had known how crowded the gym gets at 7 p.m., I would have signed up for the morning membership instead.

grammar.point: 관계부사 when · where (선행사가 시간·장소일 때, = 전치사 + which)
grammar.quote: Wednesday was a day when Korean investors finally had something to cheer about. / Thursday's trading in Seoul, where chip stocks lead the market, ...
grammar.explain_ko: 관계부사 뒤에는 주어·목적어가 빠지지 않은 '완전한 절'이 온다(investors had something / chip stocks lead the market). a day when = a day on which, Seoul, where = Seoul, in which. 뒤 절이 불완전하면(목적어가 빠지면) which, 완전하면 when/where — 이게 수능 어법 단골 포인트. 콤마 + where는 계속적 용법(서울, 그곳에서는~).
examples: I still remember the day when the KOSPI hit a circuit breaker.
(OPIc) There's a small park near my place where I usually go jogging after work.

tense.sentence: SK hynix, which reported its quarterly results that morning, surged 10.9%.
tense.why_ko: 'that morning·Wednesday'처럼 끝난 과거 시점이 분명하니 현재완료(has reported)가 아니라 단순 과거.

tense.sentence: Thursday's trading in Seoul ... may depend on which report investors take more seriously.
tense.tense: 현재 (조동사 may + 동사원형, 간접의문문 속 현재 take)
tense.why_ko: 아직 열리지 않은 목요일 장에 대한 추측이라 may + 원형. 간접의문문(which report investors take) 안은 '의문사 + 주어 + 동사' 어순이고 현재 시제로 미래를 대신한다.

review.q: The Fed decision came out at 3 a.m., but I didn't want to ______, so I waited until the market opened before buying anything.
review.exp_ko: jump the gun = 너무 성급하게 먼저 움직이다. '성급하게 굴기 싫어서 장 열릴 때까지 기다렸다'가 so 뒤 내용과 맞는다. hedge my bets(분산해 두다)·play it by ear(그때그때 정하다)는 '기다렸다'와 반대 논리가 아니고, cut it close(아슬아슬하게 하다)는 시간 여유 이야기라 문맥과 무관.

review.q: After losing badly in the first half, the team clawed back two goals before the final whistle. — 밑줄 친 부분과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: won back two goals with hard effort
review.exp_ko: claw back = (잃은 것을) 힘겹게 되찾다 → '애써 두 골을 만회했다'. ①은 오히려 더 내줬다는 뜻으로 반대, ③은 판정 이야기, ④ nearly scored는 '거의 넣을 뻔했다'라 실제로 되찾았다는 뜻이 빠진다.

review.q: Unfortunately, the extra calories from my post-workout snack ______ most of what I had burned on the treadmill.
review.exp_ko: offset = 상쇄하다. '간식 칼로리가 러닝머신에서 태운 칼로리 대부분을 상쇄했다'. outperform(~보다 낫다)은 비교 대상이 어색하고, rule out(배제하다)·take a hit(타격을 입다, 목적어 없이 씀)은 '칼로리를 지우는' 의미가 없다.

quiz.q:
[어휘] 문맥상 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
"Microsoft delivered an upside surprise. Alphabet, by contrast, ______ forecasts, with earnings of $2.12 versus $3.01, and its shares slid about 6%."
quiz.exp_ko: by contrast(반면) + 2.12달러 vs 예상 3.01달러 + 주가 하락 → '예상에 못 미쳤다' = fell short of. fell back on(~에 의지하다), fell out of(~에서 떨어져 나오다/유행이 지나다), fell in with(~와 어울리다/동의하다)는 모두 fall 구동사라 겉모습은 같지만 '숫자가 기대에 미달'이라는 뜻이 없다.

quiz.q:
[어법] 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
"Wednesday was a day ①which Korean investors finally had something to cheer about, and SK hynix, ②which reported its results that morning, surged 10.9%. If the two dissenters had won the vote, the Fed ③would have raised rates, while Microsoft's shares rose about 4% in trading ④held after the close."
quiz.exp_ko: ① 뒤 절 'Korean investors finally had something'은 주어·목적어가 다 있는 완전한 절이고 선행사 a day는 시간 → 관계부사 when(= on which)이 맞다. ② which는 뒤에 주어가 빠진 불완전한 절(reported its results)을 이끄는 계속적 용법이라 맞고, ③ If + had p.p. → would have p.p. 가정법 과거완료, ④ trading은 '열리는' 대상이라 수동 과거분사 held가 맞다.

quiz.q: [요지] 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? (본문 전체)
choices: The Fed's decision to raise rates brought the KOSPI's rally to an end.
Microsoft's strong results guarantee further gains for Korean chip stocks.
Individual investors drove the KOSPI back above the 6,000 level.
A strong day in Seoul now faces a test from mixed signals sent overnight.
quiz.exp_ko: 글은 '서울 6.6% 급등 → 그러나 미국은 불분명(동결+매파 반대표, MSFT 호실적 vs GOOGL 미달) → 목요일 장은 어느 쪽을 믿느냐에 달렸다' 구조라 ④. ① 연준은 금리를 올리지 않고 동결했다. ② 알파벳 미달이 함께 있어 '보장'은 과장. ③ 개인은 오히려 1.80조 원 순매도했다.

quiz.q: [내용 일치·추론] 본문의 내용으로 미루어 알 수 있는 것은?
choices: Alphabet missed its forecast by a smaller amount than Microsoft beat its own.
Individuals sold slightly more shares than foreigners and institutions bought combined.
SK hynix rose more than twice as much as the KOSPI did on Wednesday.
Alphabet's after-hours drop was smaller than Microsoft's after-hours gain.
quiz.exp_ko: 개인 순매도 1.80조 > 외국인+기관 순매수 1.78조 → ②. ① 알파벳 미달 폭 0.89달러(3.01−2.12) > MSFT 초과 폭 0.17달러(4.89−4.72)로 반대. ③ 코스피 6.6%의 2배는 13.2%인데 SK하이닉스는 10.9%라 2배가 안 된다. ④ 약 6% 하락 > 약 4% 상승으로 반대.

talk.topic: One beat, one miss — 빅테크 실적이 엇갈린 밤, 아침에 뭘 봐야 하나
talk.setting_ko: 목요일 아침 출근길, 투자하는 회사 동기(B)와 밤사이 연준·빅테크 실적 이야기를 나눈다.

dialogue.en: Did you stay up for the Fed last night? I passed out before 3 a.m.
dialogue.ko: 어젯밤 연준 발표 보려고 안 잤어? 난 새벽 3시 전에 뻗었어.

dialogue.en: Barely. They held rates, but two people wanted a hike, so the jury is still out on December.
dialogue.ko: 겨우 봤지. 금리는 동결인데 두 명이 인상을 원했대. 그래서 12월은 아직 몰라.

dialogue.en: And then Microsoft beat and Google missed at the same time? That's so confusing.
dialogue.ko: 그리고 마이크로소프트는 잘 나오고 구글은 못 미쳤다며? 동시에? 너무 헷갈린다.

dialogue.en: Yeah, I wouldn't overreact to the after-hours moves, though. They can cool off by the morning.
dialogue.ko: 응, 근데 시간외 움직임에 너무 과민반응하진 않을래. 아침이면 식을 수도 있거든.

dialogue.en: Honestly, after yesterday's six-percent jump, I'm thinking about taking some profits.
dialogue.ko: 솔직히 어제 6% 오른 거 보고 나니까 수익을 좀 챙길까 생각 중이야.

dialogue.en: I'm on the fence too. Maybe sell a small part and keep the rest?
dialogue.ko: 나도 고민 중이야. 조금만 팔고 나머지는 들고 갈까?

dialogue.en: That sounds reasonable. Let's see how chip stocks open first.
dialogue.ko: 그게 괜찮겠다. 일단 반도체가 어떻게 시작하는지부터 보자.

expressions.ex: The jury is still out on whether this new protein powder actually works.

expressions.when_ko: 작은 뉴스·숫자에 지나치게 반응하지 말자고 할 때
expressions.ex: Don't overreact to one bad workout — everyone has off days.
Let's wait until the hype cools off before we buy tickets.

expressions.when_ko: 오른 주식을 팔아 이익을 확정할 때
expressions.ex: After a big jump like that, a lot of people take some profits.

expressions.when_ko: 두 선택지 사이에서 고민 중일 때
expressions.ex: I'm still on the fence about renewing my gym membership.

your_turn.q_en: If a stock you own jumped 6% in one day, would you sell some of it or hold on? Why?
your_turn.hint_ko: take some profits / be on the fence / overreact to 를 써서 '내 원칙 + 이유 1개 + 예외 상황'으로 3~4문장.
your_turn.sample_answer: Honestly, I'd probably take some profits, maybe a third of it. A six-percent jump in a single day doesn't happen often, and I don't want to give it all back if the market cools off. But I wouldn't sell everything, because I'd hate to overreact to one big day if the company's story is still good. So I'd split the difference.

talk.topic: 헬스장에서 기구 같이 쓰기 — 'Can I work in with you?' (Background Survey #51 헬스)
talk.setting_ko: 퇴근 후 붐비는 헬스장. 스쿼트 랙을 한 사람(B)이 계속 쓰고 있어, A가 세트 사이에 같이 써도 되는지 묻는다.

dialogue.en: Hey, sorry to bother you. How many sets do you have left?
Two more, but I'm resting a lot between them.
dialogue.ko: 두 세트 더요. 근데 세트 사이에 많이 쉬어서요.

dialogue.en: Mind if I... actually, can I work in with you? I just need the rack for some warm-up squats.
dialogue.ko: 혹시... 아니, 사이사이 같이 써도 될까요? 워밍업 스쿼트만 좀 하면 돼서요.

dialogue.en: Sure, go for it. I'm almost done anyway. Just put the plates back to 100 when you're finished.
dialogue.ko: 그럼요, 쓰세요. 어차피 거의 끝났어요. 끝나면 원판만 100으로 다시 맞춰 주세요.

dialogue.en: No problem. Take your time on your set, I'll jump in after you.
dialogue.ko: 알겠습니다. 천천히 하세요, 끝나시면 제가 들어갈게요.

dialogue.en: Actually, could you spot me on this last one? It's a new weight for me.
dialogue.ko: 저기, 이번 마지막 세트 보조 좀 서 주실래요? 처음 드는 무게라서요.

dialogue.en: Of course. I've got you — just tell me if you want help on the way up.
dialogue.ko: 물론이죠. 제가 잡아 드릴게요 — 올라올 때 도움 필요하면 말씀하세요.

expressions.en: How many sets do you have left?
expressions.when_ko: 헬스장에서 기구를 언제 쓸 수 있는지 정중히 물을 때
expressions.ex: How many sets do you have left on the bench?

expressions.en: Can I work in with you?
expressions.when_ko: 상대가 쉬는 동안 번갈아 기구를 쓰고 싶을 때
expressions.ex: The gym was packed, so I asked a guy if I could work in with him on the leg press.

expressions.when_ko: 무거운 무게를 들 때 안전 보조를 부탁할 때
expressions.ex: I always ask someone to spot me when I go heavy on the bench press.
Take your time — I'll stretch while I wait.

expressions.when_ko: 상대 부탁을 부담 없이 들어줄 때
expressions.ex: Go ahead and use the treadmill, I'm almost done anyway.

your_turn.q_en: Have you ever had a problem with sharing equipment at the gym? What happened?
your_turn.hint_ko: 과거 시제로 '언제·어디 → 무슨 일 → 내가 한 말(Can I work in with you?) → 결과'. 근육·운동 이름(squat rack, leg press) 하나 넣기.
your_turn.sample_answer: Yeah, once at my old gym, a guy was using the squat rack for almost forty minutes, mostly just texting between sets. I was getting kind of annoyed, but I didn't want to be rude, so I asked him how many sets he had left and whether I could work in with him. He was actually really nice about it, and we ended up taking turns. Since then, I just ask politely instead of waiting around.

opic.survey_topic: 목요일 돌발 주제 — 은행·금융 생활 (서베이 #31 주식 투자와 연결)

combo.q_en: I'd like to ask you about banks in your country. What are banks like? Where are they usually located, and what do people typically do there? Please describe a bank you often go to in as much detail as possible.
combo.q_ko: 당신 나라의 은행에 대해 묻고 싶어요. 은행은 어떤 모습인가요? 보통 어디에 있고 사람들은 거기서 주로 무엇을 하나요? 자주 가는 은행을 최대한 자세히 묘사해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(한국 은행 한 줄 요약: '요즘은 앱이 기본, 지점은 줄어드는 중') → 본문 ① 위치·외관(역 근처·건물 1층, ATM 코너) ② 안에서 하는 일(번호표·창구·상담) ③ 내가 가는 이유(대출·통장 같은 앱으로 안 되는 일) → 마무리(지점은 '마지막 수단'). 90초. IH/AL 포인트: 현재 시제 일관 + 관계부사(where·when)로 문장 잇기 + 자기수정 1회.
combo.model_answer: Okay, banks in Korea. Well, these days most people do their banking on their phones, so honestly, I don't go to a branch that often. But when I do, I usually go to the one right next to the subway station near my office. It's on the first floor of a big office building, and there's a little ATM corner by the entrance where you can withdraw cash even late at night. When you walk inside, the first thing you do is grab a number ticket from a machine, and then you just sit and wait until your number shows up on the screen. There are maybe five or six tellers, and on the left side there's a separate area where you can talk to someone about loans or investment accounts. Actually, wait, I think they moved that upstairs last year. Anyway, the place is clean and quiet, kind of like a hospital waiting room, you know? I mean, it's not exciting at all, but it's where I go when the app just can't handle what I need, like opening a new account.

key_phrases.en: these days most people ~ on their phones
wait until your number shows up
when the app just can't handle ~

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 'Bank is big. I go bank.' 나열 → IH는 위치·순서(when you walk in, the first thing ~)로 공간을 따라 걷듯 묘사 → AL은 '병원 대기실 같다' 같은 비유 + 'Actually, wait,' 자기수정으로 자연스러움을 보여 준다.

combo.q_en: How have banks changed over the years? Compare the way people used banks in the past with how they use them now. What do you think caused these changes?
combo.q_ko: 은행은 몇 년 사이 어떻게 변했나요? 예전에 사람들이 은행을 이용하던 방식과 지금을 비교하고, 그 변화의 원인은 무엇이라고 생각하나요?
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(한 문장 결론: 'branch → app') → 본문 ① 과거: 부모님과 통장 들고 가서 기다리던 기억(used to) ② 현재: 송금·투자까지 앱 30초 ③ 원인 2개(스마트폰·인터넷 전문은행 경쟁) + 부작용 1개(어르신 소외) → 마무리(내 생각 한 줄). 2분. IH/AL 포인트: 과거(used to)↔현재 시제 대비, 원인-결과 연결어, 사회적 시각 한 스푼.
combo.model_answer: Oh, banks have changed a lot, like, completely. When I was a kid, my mom used to take me to the bank with this little paper bankbook, and we'd wait for, I don't know, thirty minutes just to deposit some money. Everything was done face to face. Now, though, I can send money, check my balance, or even buy stocks on my phone in about thirty seconds. I can't even remember the last time I actually used a bankbook. So why did this happen? I think there are two main reasons. First, obviously, smartphones. Once everyone had one, it just made sense to put the bank in your pocket. Second, online-only banks showed up a few years ago, and they were so easy to use that the traditional banks had no choice but to catch up. The downside, I guess, is that a lot of older people have a hard time with the apps, and as branches close, they kind of get left behind. So overall, it's way more convenient for people my age, but I do think banks should keep at least some branches open for the elderly.

key_phrases.en: my mom used to take me to ~
had no choice but to catch up

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '옛날엔 갔고 지금은 앱'만 말함 → IH는 used to + 구체 장면(종이 통장, 30분 대기) 대비 → AL은 원인 2개를 First/Second로 정리하고 '어르신 소외' 같은 사회적 반대 시각까지 붙여 균형 잡힌 의견으로 마무리.

combo.q_en: Tell me about a memorable experience you had at a bank or with a banking service. Maybe something went wrong, or something surprising happened. What happened, and how did you deal with it?
combo.q_ko: 은행이나 금융 서비스와 관련된 기억에 남는 경험을 말해 주세요. 문제가 생겼거나 놀라운 일이 있었을 수도 있죠. 무슨 일이 있었고 어떻게 해결했나요?
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(언제·무슨 일 한 줄 예고) → 본문 ① 배경(첫 주식 계좌 개설하려던 날) ② 문제(본인 인증 오류·지점 마감 직전) ③ 해결(직원 도움·다음 날 재방문) + 감정 → 마무리(배운 점, 지금과 연결). 2분. IH/AL 포인트: 과거·과거완료(had already) 정확히, 가정법 과거완료 1문장(If I had ~, I would have ~), 긴장감 있는 이야기 흐름.
combo.model_answer: Let me tell you about the day I tried to open my first stock trading account. This was maybe five years ago. I'd watched a bunch of YouTube videos, and I was super excited to finally buy my first stock. So I downloaded the app, but it kept failing at the ID verification step, like, five times in a row. I was getting really frustrated, so I rushed to the branch on my lunch break. When I got there, though, there was a huge line, and by the time it was my turn, my lunch break had already ended. I ended up coming back the next morning, right when they opened. The teller was really patient, and it turned out my phone number was still registered under my old carrier, which was why the app kept rejecting me. She fixed it in, like, ten minutes. If I had checked that first, I would have saved myself a lot of stress. But you know, it actually taught me something: before you panic, check the boring stuff first. I still use that rule, even with investing.

key_phrases.en: by the time it was my turn, ~ had already ended
key_phrases.ko: 내 차례가 됐을 땐 ~이 이미 끝나 있었다
그래서 ~였던 거다 (앞 내용 전체를 받는 이유)

key_phrases.en: If I had checked ~, I would have saved myself ~

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 사건을 한 줄로 요약 → IH는 배경-문제-해결 순서로 시간 흐름(by the time, right when)을 살림 → AL은 가정법 과거완료로 '후회'를 넣고 마지막에 교훈을 현재 습관(투자)과 연결해 이야기를 닫는다.

useful.en: So why did this happen? I think there are two main reasons.
useful.ko: 그럼 왜 이렇게 됐을까요? 이유는 크게 두 가지예요.
useful.when_ko: 비교·변화 문제에서 스스로 질문을 던지고 구조를 잡을 때

useful.ko: 그게 사실 제게 하나를 가르쳐 줬어요: ~

opic.practice_ko: 오늘은 1번(묘사)을 타이머 90초로 한 번 녹음 → 들어 보며 'when you walk in / where you can ~'으로 공간 이동이 들리는지 확인 → 3번은 'If I had ~, I would have ~' 문장만 내 경험으로 바꿔 3번 소리 내 말하기.
